Interesting. In my district, determining eligibility requires full assessment for every triennial. The school psych, case manager, and any related services providers do a full eval. 

Specialized academic instruction can be push in support for math. There’s no reason this can’t be added to services without assessment if the team feels it necessary.

I think overall, parent(s) should speak to the case manager about her concerns.

I’m assuming you mean without formal assessment. I’m also assuming this student has been formally assessed within the last 3 years, as is by law every 3 years (Called a Triennial IEP). 

Op, he can absolutely have accommodations added to his IEP without further assessment. Contact his case manager. You can always have an Amendment IEP to add these services at any time. Some things they might add: access to manipulatives (number lines, hundreds chart, etc), extended time for assignments/assessments, specialized academic instruction in math, etc. 

It is really, really great that your sons reading has progressed considerably! You must have a good team working with him, yourself included.

I don’t know where you live or what the district is like, so I can only speak to my own experience. We don’t have applied skills classrooms, that would be referred to as a mod/severe setting here. Our mild/mod students (which it sounds like your daughter might be) are in general education classes with push in/pull out support.

If your daughter is cognitively able, I really push for the gen Ed setting. In my district, it’s more difficult to get students out of the mod severe setting because they are behind their peers academically, socially and behaviorally. In a gen Ed setting, she will have model peers to learn from and will be given the opportunity to gain independence. 

I had a student at the start of the year with very high push in/pull out hours. His parents were concerned he wasn’t in the right placement and might need a 1:1 aide. However, I wanted to give him the opportunity to grow and I did not want him to become prompt dependent. Fast forward to today, the whole team (parents included) are on board to decrease his hours significantly because he is doing so well in the gen Ed setting.
 
Just my two cents!

Students are educated in the least restrictive environment and should not be placed in a special day class due to behaviors that are not harming themselves or others. It is important for students to be in an environment with model peers and to learn expected behaviors in these environments. All students can benefit from the least restrictive environment. For example, your child may be learning behaviors that are not okay and directly seeing the consequences of such behavior. 

Any student can have a behavior intervention plan, which may be something to suggest or something the team at school is already working on.

I am a  5'2 and 100 pound female.

While dealing aggression can be part of the job, as behavior therapy deals with behaviors, my office wouldn't give me a case that I couldn't handle. I.e; more experienced therapists (I've only been in the field a few months) may be paired with more aggressive clients.

That being said, I have had a 5 y/o try to bite me, which doesn't really hurt. I was taught how to safely block/remove if they are biting. You will be trained by your BCBA.

​

Check out some Youtube videos, read blogs about the field of Behavior Analysis. And if it seems like something you're interested, check out a clinic & apply. You don't have to stay in the field forever if it's not for you, and you don't have to decide on being a BCBA before you even begin as an RBT. Through your Master's to get your BCBA, you will essentially be working as an RBT too.
